newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB says ready to boost Asian investment.
newsitem.headline: NAB says ready to boost Asian investment.

text.p: Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB), said on Thursday its Asian strategy was key to its global plans and the bank was now in a position to increase its investment in the region.

Delivering the annual Asialink lecture, NAB's managing director and chief executive Don Argus said the bank had adopted a strategy of building up its global network and core business competancies before starting a significant push into Asia.
"We are now able to attune our services to the specific needs of the region and progressively increase our overall investment and overall involvement," Argus said.
Argus said the bank was aware of its limitations in terms of knowledge and experience in Asia but was intent on progressively building its expertise and reputation.

"It is the utilisation of our core strengths in areas such as treasury operations and home mortgages - services that are common throughout our group that have proved early success for us in Asia," he said.
Argus said the Asian market was a good indicator of global trends and had a base of core values that were common across its international businesses.
NAB employs about 280 staff in its Asian division which more than doubled its earnings to A$15 million in the six months to March 31, 1997, compared to A$6 million a year earlier.
The bank's regional head office is based in Hong Kong and has five branches and five representative offices in 10 of the region's major banking and financial services markets.
